name: temperature
description: Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold an object is, reflecting the average kinetic energy of its particles. It is commonly measured in degrees using scales such as Celsius (°C) and Fahrenheit (°F) and indicates the direction of heat flow between objects.

name: rainfall
description: Rainfall is the amount of water that falls to the ground as precipitation, typically measured in inches or centimeters. It is a crucial part of the Earth's water cycle, replenishing lakes, rivers, and groundwater, and supporting plant and animal life.

name: air_quality
description: Air quality refers to the condition of the air in our environment, specifically how clean or polluted it is. It is measured using the Air Quality Index (AQI), which indicates the level of pollutants like ozone, particulate matter, and nitrogen dioxide, and can affect human health and the environment.

name: co2_levels
description: Carbon dioxide (CO2) levels in the atmosphere are a key factor in weather and climate. Higher CO2 concentrations, which have increased significantly since the Industrial Revolution, contribute to the greenhouse effect, trapping heat and leading to changes in weather patterns, including more extreme weather events.

name: humidity
description: Humidity is the measure of water vapor present in the air, which can affect weather conditions and how comfortable it feels outside. It is typically expressed as relative humidity, a percentage that compares the current amount of water vapor in the air to the maximum amount the air can hold at a given temperature.
